images.title: Does the tool earn its place?
images.alt: Decision chart: if checking AI output is quicker than doing the task yourself, keep the tool; if not, do the work yourself.
images.caption: AI tools give a fast first version, so the real cost is the time it takes you to check it.

images.title: From AI answer to a fact you can repeat
images.alt: Four steps for AI research: get an answer with links, open each source, find the exact sentence, and prefer the original source.
images.caption: Treat an AI answer as a faster route to sources, then read the sources.

items.title: Get an answer with links
items.text: Use a tool that searches the web and shows the pages it used.

items.title: Open the source
items.text: A citation can point to a page that doesn't say what the answer claims.

items.title: Find the sentence
items.text: Locate the exact line that supports the claim before you repeat it.

items.title: Prefer the original
items.text: The company's terms page, the regulator or the study beats a blog post about it.

images.title: Why automation needs a different safeguard
images.alt: Comparison of drafting with an assistant, where you see every output, and automation, where one wrong output can repeat for weeks.
images.caption: Keep a manual approval step in front of anything an automation publishes or sends to a customer.
